adversarial_probes.name: R-2 live: genesis-owner org-set does NOT reach a NEW root department
adversarial_probes.setup: Added a 4th root (newroot, parent_id NULL) to the org oracle; the seed's owner org-set ceiling is {fin,cs,plat}.
adversarial_probes.result: behavior pinned — three honest framings recorded for handoff
adversarial_probes.findings: a1: owner (isGenesisOwner=true) delegating onto newroot is ACCEPTED — the owner short-circuit (FR-4) BYPASSES the org gate, so owner reach is NOT limited by the seeded set; the set only bounds DOWNSTREAM admins. a2: a delegated (non-owner) admin whose ceiling is {fin,cs,plat} is REJECTED (org_scope_widens) on newroot — this is the real R-2 limitation: forest-wide reach delegated FROM the owner is pinned to the 3-root snapshot. a3: resource-axis — a child grant whose scope=newroot is NOT ⊑ the owner's {fin,cs,plat} grant-set (scope_widens). HANDOFF: R-2 is a genuine forward-limitation for T-0030/T-0053 (re-broaden owner grant-set or revisit super-root when a new root is minted), but NOT a self-elevation hole: the owner himself, being the un-parented root, can always mint authority on a new root; only authority he has already DELEGATED down stays pinned. No code defect.
adversarial_probes.verdict: expected / by-design; R-2 confirmed as forward-limitation, not a defect

adversarial_probes.name: Set-widening: one member wider, rest already-covered → reject (no averaging)
adversarial_probes.setup: Admin grant/ceiling scope = org-set {fin,cs}; child delegation org-set = {fin,plat} (fin covered, plat escapes).
adversarial_probes.result: rejected on BOTH axes — no partial/average acceptance
adversarial_probes.findings: org-axis: {fin,plat} not ⊑ {fin,cs} → org_scope_widens (fires first). With ceiling widened to isolate the resource axis: child grant-set {fin,plat} not ⊑ admin grant-set {fin,cs} → scope_widens. The WHOLE set is rejected when ANY single member escapes; the subset gate has no notion of 'most members fit'.
adversarial_probes.verdict: expected / by-design — set containment is all-members, no averaging

adversarial_probes.name: isGenesisOwner=true + garbage target — trust-boundary honesty
adversarial_probes.setup: Owner flag injected true; targets = freeform child with a FOREIGN tenant_id in the field + empty-set org; and a bogus resourceType 'mgmt_object:NONSENSE' onto an unknown org node.
adversarial_probes.result: owner bypass is TOTAL and is the FLAG, not the input — trust boundary is the caller
adversarial_probes.findings: c1/c2: with isGenesisOwner=true the checker returns {ok:true} for freeform-garbage and for bogus-resourceType/unknown-node children alike — it validates NOTHING once the owner flag is set (intended un-parented-root semantics, FR-4). c3: the SAME bogus child as a NON-owner is rejected (org_scope_widens) — proving the bypass is driven by the injected flag, not by anything in the target. TRUST BOUNDARY (handoff): the pure checker is correctly ignorant of 'owner'; the security of isGenesisOwner rests ENTIRELY on the CALLER (T-0030 write-API) deriving it from the seeded tenant-owner role + confirmed in-window genesis assignment. A caller that sets the flag from untrusted input would be a full self-elevation hole — but that surface is T-0030, not T-0029. The checker also does NOT validate childGrant.tenantId against the admin's tenant — cross-tenant safety is enforced by RLS at the DB write-path (T-0030/T-0053), not the pure checker. Honest, documented boundary; no defect in T-0029's surface.
adversarial_probes.verdict: honest bypass / boundary documented — no hole in T-0029; flag-derivation security is T-0030's contract (frozen NF-7)

adversarial_probes.name: Seed re-entrancy: delete a mgmt-grant, re-run migrations → NOT restored
adversarial_probes.setup: On the isolated DB after a clean seed (17 grants), manually DELETE one mgmt-grant (the invoke grant e1000000-…-0011), then re-run node migrations/run.mjs.
adversarial_probes.result: NOT restored — count stays 16 after re-run
adversarial_probes.findings: The runner records version '026_genesis_owner_seed' in schema_migrations and SKIPS already-recorded versions — the file SQL is never re-executed on a normal re-run, so a row deleted AFTER seeding is NOT reconciled back. This is BY DESIGN and consistent with the spec: FR-5/AC-12 promise 're-running the migration set yields identical row counts' (true: a normal re-run is a no-op, counts unchanged), NOT self-healing of post-seed drift. Layer-2 probe (ADV-d-bis): clearing the bookkeeping row forces 026 pending → file re-executes, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING re-asserts the missing grant (→17) and creates NO duplicates. So 'idempotency' here = (1) bookkeeping skip on normal re-run + (2) ON CONFLICT safety on forced replay; it is explicitly NOT reconciliation. Matches runner contract (migrations/run.mjs header) and spec intent.
adversarial_probes.verdict: expected / by-design — idempotency != reconciliation; spec-consistent, no defect
